tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local positive-control fixture continuing the prior atomic-coupling negative control. Abstract effect E has current authoritative claim incarnation B={F_new,T_new}; stale A={F_old,T_old} is no longer authoritative. The modeled transport exposes one indivisible conditional mutation whose predicate requires current claim identity to equal the caller's expected {fence,token} and effect E to be uncommitted; on success it commits E and an idempotency marker together. Interleaving tested: stale A attempts first, current B attempts second, then B retries once. No public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, real external coordinator, richer-mode arbitration, or optional second semantic leaf was used.

fixture.atomic_primitive: commit E iff current claim identity == expected {fence,token} AND E is uncommitted; authority predicate evaluation, effect write and idempotency marker write are one indivisible operation
interleaving: 1. A invokes the conditional mutation with expected {F_old,T_old}; current authority is {F_new,T_new}, so predicate is false and A performs no mutation.
2. B invokes the same conditional mutation with expected {F_new,T_new}; authority matches and E is uncommitted, so B commits E and its idempotency marker exactly once.
3. B retries with the same expected identity; authority still matches but E is already committed, so the uncommitted predicate is false and no duplicate mutation occurs.

required_assumptions: claim identity comparison and effect mutation are atomic together
fence/token incarnation is non-reusable for the claim lifetime
effect committed marker participates in the same atomic decision

observations: A cannot use a cached earlier validation because the authority predicate is evaluated inside the same indivisible operation that would mutate E.
B can commit once because its expected identity matches the current claim and E is initially uncommitted.
B's retry cannot duplicate E because the same atomic predicate also requires E to remain uncommitted.
inference: Within this exact abstract fixture, an atomic conditional effect primitive over both current non-reusable claim identity and an uncommitted effect marker is sufficient to reject the tested stale-incarnation interleaving and the tested same-incarnation retry while permitting one current commit. This proves only the modeled safety/idempotency property. It does not prove that any concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport exposes the primitive, that claim acquisition is single-winner, that coupled state survives interruption, or that the mechanism is live or fork-safe under real contention.

Atomic single-winner claim acquisition keyed by stable effect identity remains unverified on a concrete allowed transport.
Interruption durability, fork exclusion and liveness under real contention remain unverified.
